domestication.def: The slow change of wild plants and animals into crops and livestock, as people chose which ones to plant or breed over many generations.

first-agricultural-revolution.def: The shift from hunting and gathering to farming that began about 12,000 to 10,000 years ago in several hearths; also called the Neolithic Revolution.

fertile-crescent.def: An arc of land in Southwest Asia, from the eastern Mediterranean along the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, where wheat, barley, sheep and goats were among the first species domesticated.

columbian-exchange.def: The transfer of plants, animals, diseases and people between the Americas and Africa, Europe and Asia that began after Columbus crossed the Atlantic in 1492.
